question_record.context: A suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine `vnevado-win11u`, which is frequently used by malware to spawn new processes and further infect a system. This incident is connected with various malicious activities executed by processes such as `vssblatemp.exe` and `get-userprttoken.ps1` on the same host. The initial indicator of compromise included a command executed by `curl` to access an external URL. This incident aligns with known tactics of cybercriminal groups, particularly the Manatee Tempest activity group, which is a Russia-based group active since 2014 and notorious for spreading malware like the Dridex banking trojan among others.
question_record.question: Can you identify the IP address associated with an activity linked to the Manatee Tempest group?
solution: A suspicious WMI process creation was detected on the machine associated with the user having AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.

The IP address `198.43.121.209` is linked to the cybercriminal group Manatee Tempest, which engages in a variety of malicious activities including drive-by downloads, malvertising, FakeUpdates (SocGholish) infections, BLISTER loader deployment, and usage of Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment.

75.name: Manatee Tempest activity group
75.description:
The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport
